transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-23
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miles Carter (Redwood CSM), Sophie Grant (Mercury Labs - Head of ML), Marcus Hsu (Eng Mgr), Leah Ortiz (FinOps), Tom Reynolds (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may have errors): QBR-style checkin, heavy focus on Feb spike, need pilot to validate dedicated capacity economics.

00:00 Jordan: All right good morning everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: recap Feb spike, cost/usage, stability notes, pilot proposal, security.
00:18 Sophie: yeah thanks jordan, i pulled in the finance team cause the burn in feb was bigger than we expected, um, and we need clarity on what drove the token increase.
00:27 Jordan: understood. priya and i will go through the telemetry, there's a couple of areas — model rollouts and cache miss rates — that look suspicious.
00:42 Priya: hey, quick note — some of the logs still tag the model as "redwood_lite" instead of the exact variant so bucketization is noisy, that may explain the label mismatch you'll see in the CSV.
00:58 Marcus: yep we saw that, the dashboards had multiple small peaks and one big spike on 2/25 around 03:20 UTC which correlated with a bot-driven test from an internal team.
01:15 Jordan: that aligns. on the big spike, there were two compounding issues: prefix cache invalidation when you switched model family, and a short-lived routing fallback to higher-cost hosted variant.
01:34 Leah: when you say "higher-cost hosted variant" do you mean the fallback to the gen-xl instance? our bill showed a big jump for gen-xl tokens.
01:44 Priya: yes — there was an automated fallback policy that moved traffic to the higher-capacity model during a short overload; latency SLOs were preserved but cost jumped.
01:59 Sophie: hmm okay, we need more control there; we can't have finance surprised like that.
02:06 Miles: to be clear we can change the fallback to cap spend or prefer degraded latency over cost — that's a policy knob you can set per-route.
02:21 Tom: can we set an emergency throttle that drops to cached responses first?
02:28 Priya: you could — prefix/KV caching is working but depends on request patterns. in your case the bot had ephemeral prefixes so the KV cache miss rate was high.
02:43 Marcus: i'm curious about batching — are we losing out by using single-request low-latency config?
02:50 Jordan: good question. based on session traces, 70% of requests were small single-turn questions, so batching improvements would help on throughput but might bump tail latency.
03:05 Leah: finance would accept a small latency increase if that reduces unit cost by 20% — what's realistic?
03:13 Priya: with a quantized 4-bit config and optimized batching we typically see 15-30% cost reduction on gen workloads, but throughput profiles matter. we'll propose a realistic number after a spike test.
03:31 Sophie: speaking of quantization, any risks to quality there? we can't degrade RAG results for customer-facing flows.
03:40 Priya: there's a tradeoff — for summarization/embedding paths quant can be safe, but for multi-turn creative generation we recommend A/B test prompts. we'll include evals in the pilot.
03:54 Jordan: proposed pilot: 6 weeks, small dedicated pool (reserved), run shadow traffic on dedicated w/ quantized variant for non-critical paths, measure latency, quality metrics, and unit cost.
04:10 Tom: how big a reserved pool are we talking? what's the commit?
04:16 Jordan: initial suggestion is 2 x A100-equivalent units with autoscale headroom for bursts. we can baseline with 1 and bump to 2 if the spike reproduces.
04:27 Leah: need cost numbers. share exact commit price and per-token deltas so finance can OK it.
04:34 Jordan: sure will send a breakdown. we'll include potential savings vs current hosted fallback as scenario A/B.
04:42 Marcus: can we run a repro spike to validate cache behaviour? i can run the bot test from our staging — good to do it with you watching.
04:51 Priya: absolutely — we'll schedule a 1-hr run, collect traces and KV cache hit/miss tables, and examine routing decisions.
05:05 Sophie: okay that's key. also security: the VP wants SOC2 evidence and to ensure KMS is used for keys.
05:14 Miles: we have SOC2 + ISO docs; i'll drop the latest artifact. for KMS we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS/HSM in private deployments and can integrate with cloud KMS for Dedicated.
05:29 Tom: what's the path if we need VPC/private deployment? we can't put production PII through hosted.
05:36 Jordan: two paths: Redwood Dedicated in a managed network with private peering or Redwood Private for a VPC/on-prem package. Dedicated gives isolation and reserved GPUs; Private puts the control plane in your VPC.
05:49 Tom: any difference in feature set?
05:52 Priya: mostly parity on inference runtime, but Private gives greater control over KMS and audit logs location. Dedicated is faster to spin up and still supports customer KMS in many cases.
06:05 Leah: audit logs — can we get token-level billing and per-route latency traces?
06:11 Miles: yes, console exposes per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns; we can also push raw logs to your SIEM via S3/Kinesis if needed.
06:24 Sophie: great. ok on the security checklist: SOC2 artifact, KMS integration guide, SSO/SAML setup — please send.
06:32 Miles: will do, i already added that to action items.
06:36 Marcus: one more technical — we saw a KV cache evict pattern after our model switch; is there a recommended migration strategy to avoid mass cache invalidations?
06:45 Priya: yes: staged rollouts and static prompt prefixes for a short window, plus priming the cache with warmup requests before cutting over. we can script the warmup.
06:58 Sophie: what's the SLA look like for Dedicated? we need to present uptime/latency to our ops team.
07:05 Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets based on the reserved pool. we'll include an SLA excerpt in the doc pack.
07:13 Tom: and fallback policies if regional capacity hits? we can't be forced to global fallback without prior approval.
07:20 Jordan: we can set region affinity and fallback tiers; we'll propose a policy that avoids cross-region fallback unless you opt-in.
07:29 Leah: finance question again — if we move to reserved, do we lose elasticity cost benefits?
07:36 Jordan: reserved gives predictable unit cost and capacity; you trade off some burstiness. we can add burst credits to handle spikes so you don't overcommit.
07:46 Marcus: sounds like a plan. schedule for the spike run?
07:51 Priya: how about next Tuesday 3/30 15:00 UTC — we can run the bot test and capture traces.
07:58 Marcus: that works for staging.
08:02 Jordan: ok set. we'll also run latency traces on p4d vs A40 equiv to show raw tail numbers.
08:11 Tom: one more vendor question — Sophie asked if competitors were cheaper or had better tooling.
08:17 Sophie: i've looked at Anthropic and Replicate; Replicate had cheaper burst rates but less mature SLA/observability.
08:27 Jordan: noted, our play is predictable economics + first-class tracing + rollout controls. we'll show a direct $/1M token comparison in the cost pack.
08:40 Miles: quick note: expect the doc pack to include per-route token burn, model variant delta, SLA excerpt, SOC2 pdf, KMS integration notes, and pilot scope.
08:53 Leah: perfect. timeline recap?
09:00 Jordan: recap: Jordan to send usage & cost breakdown by Fri 3/26; Miles to send SOC2 + security pack by Thu 3/25; Priya to run spike on Tue 3/30 and share traces; customer to confirm pilot metrics by Tue 3/29.
09:18 Sophie: yes, and please call out a realistic savings estimate not just optimistic upper bounds.
09:24 Priya: we'll include best-case / expected / conservative bands.
09:30 Tom: ok thanks, that's good coverage. any other questions?
09:35 Marcus: none here.
09:38 Jordan: all right we'll follow up in the thread with scheduling and artifacts. thanks everyone.
09:45 (meeting ends)
